One configurable Gimble instance hosts simultaneous runs and conversations for multiple projects, with project-local durable state; another independently configured instance can coexist. Treat coherence and simplicity for one local user as the priority, not security hardening.

Project identity is consistent across CLI inputs, browser paths, run lists, streams, controls, conversations, and reopened history. Ordinary path aliases do not create duplicate project state, and selecting one project never shows or controls another project's runs.

The ordinary gimble run CLI submits built-in workflows to the selected persistent instance without starting another runtime. A run is observable there and its CLI-supplied choices remain meaningful; inherited executables and provider configuration come from the instance startup environment, as documented in CLI help.

Conversation agents launch workflows through that same CLI, not a conversation-only structured workflow response or direct-launch callback. A conversation's owning project remains distinct from its execution worktree, and its run link and terminal status survive a page reload.
